lines.text: In the Mariana Trench, where pressure would crush a steel submarine, what bizarre creatures actually survive?
Under crushing pressure and freezing darkness, life has adapted in terrifying ways.
The Mariana snailfish lives five miles deep, having completely scaleless gelatinous tissue to resist pressure.
Giant amphipods grow to the size of dinner plates, feeding on dead whale carcasses sinking from above.
Deep sea anglerfish illuminate pitch black waters with glowing bioluminescent bacterial lures on their foreheads.
Many deep-sea animals don't have eyes at all, navigating by sensing water pressure vibrations.
The bottom of our ocean feels closer to another planet than planet Earth.
